title: The Late Witness
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Vane, founder of the cathedral town of Marrow's Bend, is exhumed for a centenary ceremony, archivist Beatrix Ashgrove discovers it empty — and finds her own handwriting in a decades-old case file she never wrote. As a modern killer begins silencing the town's elders in the order of a ledger Beatrix keeps, she realizes the founder never died: he vanished in 1924, assumed a new identity, and someone now protecting his secret is willing to murder to keep the crypt locked. Beatrix, an orphan who built herself a family among the cathedral staff, must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy her found family and letting a killer walk free; she stages a false exhumation to trap the killer — the cathedral's own dean, who is the founder's grandson — and testifies at trial as the late witness the dead never got to be.
about_author: Hazel Brightwater is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of small-town secrets before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet people who keep dangerous archives, from a stone cottage she shares with an ill-tempered cat named Folio.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. During the centenary exhumation of founder Aldous Vane, the coffin proves empty except for a brass key and a scrap of ledger paper. Beatrix, whose job is order, feels her ordered world crack. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Beatrix searches the cathedral archive for exhumation records and finds a 1924 case file annotated in handwriting identical to her own. POV shifts briefly to Detective Ilsa Reyes, skeptical of the 'archivist coincidence.' Emotional beat: uncanny recognition.

chapters.title: The Dean's Kindness
chapters.summary: Dean Edmund Vane, the founder's great-grandson and Beatrix's mentor, soothes the town and quietly asks Beatrix to 'lose' the 1924 file. Her POV. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by instinct.

chapters.title: First Silence
chapters.summary: Retired sexton Harold Pike — the first name on the old ledger — is found dead in the bell tower, staged as a fall. Beatrix realizes the deaths may follow the ledger's alphabetical order. Her POV. Emotional beat: guilt, because she catalogued the list.

chapters.title: A Family of Strangers
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Beatrix's POV: how she arrived in Marrow's Bend an orphan and was folded into the cathedral staff — the dean, the organist, the housekeeper — her found family. Emotional beat: warmth that raises the stakes of every suspicion.

chapters.title: The Key That Fits
chapters.summary: Beatrix secretly tries the coffin's brass key on the crypt's inner door; it fits a lock installed in 1924, after Vane's supposed burial. Reyes's POV, watching Beatrix from the shadows. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming.

chapters.title: Second on the List
chapters.summary: Organist Marguerite Cole, the ledger's next living name, receives a threatening note written in Beatrix's forged hand. Marguerite confronts Beatrix; their friendship frays. Marguerite's POV. Emotional beat: betrayal before any betrayal occurs.

chapters.title: The Forger's Lesson
chapters.summary: Beatrix studies the forged documents and realizes the forger trained on her own archival hand — someone with years of access. She narrows suspects to staff. Her POV. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: What Harold Knew
chapters.summary: Reyes and Beatrix exhume Pike's past: in 1924 he saw Aldous Vane alive, weeks after the funeral, boarding a train under a new name. Reyes's POV. Emotional beat: the thrill of a case turning real.

chapters.title: The Vanished Founder
chapters.summary: Beatrix traces Vane's new identity through shipping manifests: he became a wealthy benefactor whose donations built half the town — including the cathedral school where the dean was raised. Her POV. Emotional beat: history as a trap.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Silence
chapters.summary: Marguerite is found drowned in the baptistry, ledger page pinned to her robe. The town turns on Beatrix, whose handwriting marked the page. Her POV. Emotional beat: isolation inside her own family.

chapters.title: Arrested Archive
chapters.summary: Reyes, under pressure, must treat Beatrix as a suspect; the dean offers Beatrix an alibi that is a lie, which she recognizes. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: protection that feels like ownership.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt Opens
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Reyes break into the crypt's inner chamber and find it furnished — a room someone has lived in, recently, with the 1924 file's missing pages. Beatrix's POV. Emotional beat: the past is not past.

chapters.title: Grandson of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Reyes uncovers the dean's true lineage: Aldous Vane faked his death, lived under a second name, and his grandson Edmund inherited both the fortune and the secret. Reyes's POV. Emotional beat: horror wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: The dean confesses partially to Beatrix: his grandfather's survival required the elders' silence, and the last living witness, housekeeper Ada Quill, is next. He asks Beatrix — family — to look away. Her POV. Emotional beat: love weaponized.

chapters.title: Ada's Choice
chapters.summary: Ada, knowing she is next, hides the ledger's final page inside the organ and gives Beatrix her testimony to carry. Ada's POV. Emotional beat: courage in an old woman who chose found family too.

chapters.title: Framing the Archivist
chapters.summary: The dean plants evidence framing Beatrix for both murders; she is arrested days before the trial. Reyes's POV, doubting the too-neat case. Emotional beat: the system closing on the innocent.

chapters.title: The False Exhumation
chapters.summary: Released on Reyes's gambit, Beatrix announces a second exhumation of the empty coffin, baiting the dean into destroying the crypt evidence before trial. Her POV. Emotional beat: the hunted setting the trap.

chapters.title: Night in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Climax: the dean comes to burn the crypt, catches Beatrix waiting, and nearly kills her; Reyes and Ada's hidden testimony recording turn the trap. The dean is taken alive among his grandfather's bones-that-never-were. Beatrix's POV. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Late Witness
chapters.summary: Trial chapter: Beatrix testifies, reading the dead elders' testimony aloud as 'the late witness' for those who died unheard. The dean is convicted. Courtroom texture, Beatrix's POV. Emotional beat: grief given a voice.

chapters.title: Reordering
chapters.summary: Beatrix recatalogues the archive, deciding some secrets deserve open shelves: she publishes the truth of Vane's vanishing. The town reels; the cathedral staff splinters. Her POV. Emotional beat: the cost of truth.

chapters.title: What Remains Filed
chapters.summary: Resolution: Beatrix, Ada, and Reyes share a quiet supper in the archive — a smaller, truer found family. She leaves one drawer empty, labeled for whatever comes next. Her POV. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, vigilance intact.
